lines.text: Line one hundred seventy-two, speed now: the length of the last command. Two meters per second.
Line one hundred seventy-three, braking distance: distance, minus speed times reaction time, minus switch radius.
Three, minus two times zero point zero five: two point nine meters. The max stops it going negative.
Lines one hundred seventy-four and seventy-five: the trapezoid rule from the board, capped at max speed.
The square root of twelve times two point nine is five point nine. Capped: four.
Line one hundred seventy-six: end speed is zero, so the gentle line applies.
K P times distance is eighteen. Four is smaller, so speed stays four.
Line one hundred seventy-eight: under three millimeters? No.
Lines one hundred eighty-two and eighty-three turn speed into an arrow.
The arrow to the goal, divided by its length, has length one. Times speed: v x and v y.
v x is four, v y is zero: straight at the goal, at top speed.
We're going two and asking for four. Can we get it? Not decided yet.
